course_name_original: DESIGN AND MANAGEMENT OF PRODUCTION SYSTEMS
course_name_en: DESIGN AND MANAGEMENT OF PRODUCTION SYSTEMS
prerequisites: Preliminary knowledge about the main manufacturing technologies used in the manufacturing sector and mechanical design.
Knowledge of basic computer skills, such as flow diagrams and the development of simple procedures.

learning_outcomes.text: Provide the fundamental elements related to the sizing and management of mechanical industrial plants.

Examine the main performance parameters of these systems, different layout configurations, procurement techniques, and methodologies for the operational management of resources within a modern system for the production of goods and services.

Acquire knowledge relating to the design process, including methods for calculating the characteristic parameters of production systems, criteria for selecting the optimal layout type, for sizing production resources, and for evaluating the economic viability of investments.

Acquire knowledge related to management processes, including criteria for identifying bottlenecks, for calculating industrial product costs, for managing material procurement, for characterizing the components of lead time, for optimizing the use of human resources, for studying work times and methods, and for managing maintenance – including types of maintenance policies and their respective areas of application.
Define the optimal layout and sizing of production resources and their efficiency.
Apply the main replenishment procurement techniques.
Identify standard times and the number of operators required in production processes.
Independently formulate the layout of an industrial plant and apply appropriate management techniques in the presence of the studied problems.
Effectively communicate on topics related to the configuration of an industrial plant and the main management problems.
Independently learn more in-depth and specific competencies in the field of design and management of industrial plants.

syllabus_topics: Classification of industrial plants and processes
Continuous and manufacturing processes, with technical fixed cycle or not, technology and service facilities, rigid and flexible automation
Characteristic parameters of the production systems: Capacity, hourly production, efficiency, vertical and horizontal integration, break even point, elasticity, versatility and flexibility
Layout study: Layout with fixed location, flow-shop, job-shop, and machining cells
Sizing of plant resources in the different configurations: Machinery, service plants, warehouses, internal transport systems
Analysis of the convenience of industrial investment: Payback period, net present value
Production system management: Potentiality, service level, yield

Material management: Lead time, materials with dependent and independent demand, bill of material, ABC analysis, economic order quantity and economic production quantity, security stocks, supplier choice, major procedures at active and passive cycle

Human resource management: Time-and-method procedure, flowcharts, two-hand diagrams, inductive and deductive methods, standard time, man-machine diagram, worker multiple management, principles of ergonomics
Maintenance: Maintenance policies and related fields of use, reliability and costs
assessment_rules: For the Design Module, a written exam (30 minutes, max 30 points) with a minimum score of 18/30 is required for admission to the oral exam (2 topics, max 30 points). The final grade for the Design Module is a weighted average of written (1/3) and oral (2/3) grades. For the Management Module, a written exam (60 minutes, variable questions on 3 topics, max 30 points) with a minimum score of 18/30 is required for admission to the oral exam. The final grade for the Management Module is a weighted average of written (8/10) and oral (2/10) grades. The overall exam grade is the average of the grades from both modules. Honors are awarded if a score of 30 is achieved in both modules, and honors are awarded in at least one of the modules.
